sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly Pteranodon character. Draw this exact Pteranodon character as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the plump body with its soft cream chest and lilac back and sides, as in image 1, without head, neck, wings or legs; its top, normally under the neck, rounded, and its bottom, where the legs join, rounded.
2. the head with its neck, as one piece: the lilac head with its long swept-back crest (pink-red at its tip, with darker lilac spots), the rosy cheek, turned to the left as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no eyebrows, no beak, no mouth line — keep the rosy cheek; where the beak would be, the face is rounded off smoothly; the cream throat and lilac back of the neck carry on down below the head, as wide as the neck is in image 1, for about half the head's height, with no chin line, and end in a smooth rounded bottom edge with no line across it.
3. the near folded wing (the one on the right in image 1): the lilac wing with its paler pink membrane and darker spots, folded down at the side as in image 1, drawn whole, its top shoulder end a smooth rounded edge.
4. the far folded wing (the one on the left in image 1): the narrower lilac wing with its pink membrane, folded down at the other side as in image 1, drawn whole, its top shoulder end a smooth rounded edge.
5. the near wing open: the same near wing spread out wide and high as in gliding flight, reaching out to the right like a big soft kite, its lilac front edge and pale pink membrane with darker spots, a smooth rounded shoulder end at its root on the left.
6. the far wing open: the same wing of the other side spread out wide as in gliding flight, reaching out to the left, seen a little shorter as it is farther away, a smooth rounded shoulder end at its root on the right.
7. the far leg: a short lilac leg with its little three-toed foot, as the left leg in image 1, drawn whole from the top of the thigh, with a rounded top.
8. the near leg: a short lilac leg with its little three-toed foot, as the right leg in image 1, drawn whole from the top of the thigh, with a rounded top.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge with no line across it. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly Pteranodon character; image 2 shows the same Pteranodon cut into puppet parts, with a blank face and no beak. Draw the Pteranodon's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Pteranodon in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching.
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye on the left in image 1, near the beak's base), each with its iris looking to the left as in image 1:
1. the far eye as it is in image 1: a dark brown oval eye with a white sparkle.
2. the same far eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same far eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few small lashes.
4. the same far eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc with a few small lashes.
5. the same far eye sad: open, the brown eye looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
6. the same far eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye on the right in image 1), each with its iris looking to the left as in image 1:
7. the near eye as it is in image 1: a big dark brown oval eye with a white sparkle.
8. the same near eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
9. the same near eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few small lashes.
10. the same near eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc with a few small lashes.
11. the same near eye sad: open, the brown eye looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
12. the same near eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 3, the brows: 13. the far eye's short thin brown brow arc as in image 1; 14. the near eye's short thin brown brow arc as in image 1; 15. the far brow sad, tilted up towards the middle of the face; 16. the near brow sad, tilted up towards the middle of the face.
Row 4, the long pointed beak, pointing to the left as in image 1, the lilac upper beak and the cream lower beak, its base on the right a smooth rounded edge with no line across it (it tucks onto the face), with the smiling mouth line curling up at the corner as in image 1:
17. the beak closed, smiling, as in image 1.
18. the same beak open wide in a happy laugh: the upper beak lifted, the inside smooth and pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth at all.
19. the same beak closed, sad: its mouth line turning down at the corner.
20. the same beak a little open in surprise: a small round opening near the corner, smooth and pink inside, no teeth.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the pteranodon flies along to the left on big slow wingbeats, gliding between them, then glides down and lands.
the pteranodon hops along to the left on its two little feet, wings folded, then stops.
the pteranodon spreads its big wings and flaps them slowly, its feet staying on the ground.

pause.shows: the pteranodon with its big wings spread wide

animations.description: the pteranodon stretches up tall and opens both its big wings out wide, holds them there, then folds them away.

pause.shows: the pteranodon standing tall with both wings stretched out wide

animations.description: the pteranodon lifts its head and calls out happily, its beak wide open, twice.

pause.shows: the pteranodon calling out happily, its head up and its beak open

animations.description: the pteranodon tucks its beak down against its wing and tidies it, nibble-nibble, then fluffs up and smooths itself down.

pause.shows: the pteranodon with its beak tucked against its wing, tidying it

animations.description: the pteranodon spreads its big wings wide and glides, floating gently up and down on the air.

pause.shows: the pteranodon gliding with its big wings spread wide

animations.description: the pteranodon bends down and pecks at the ground with its long beak, peck-peck-peck, then looks up happily.

pause.shows: the pteranodon bent forward, its beak down to the ground

animations.description: the pteranodon crouches, jumps up high for joy with its wings out and lands with a little squash.
the pteranodon shakes its head no.
the pteranodon looks up, then turns right round to look behind it, then turns back and looks ahead again.

pause.shows: the pteranodon turned round, looking behind it

animations.description: the pteranodon cries, head down, its shoulders shaking with little sobs.

pause.shows: the pteranodon crying, head down, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the pteranodon lifts its big wing and waves hello.
